chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Summers sitting in around Richmond; Bessie Smith at the Hippodrome
summary: In summers he sat in with Johnson's Happy Pals and heard Bessie Smith at the Hippodrome Theater.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: In the summers I started in -- started playing in the band around this school. In the summers I would go around Richmond which was 40 miles away. And at that time around Richmond there was a band that was kind of popular, Johnson's Happy Pals. And Roy Johnson and a bunch of them had this band together. They played a lot of blues, and they played a lot of other things. They played dances around there.
So, I'd sit in with them several times. I didn't know too much about what I was doing but I had a lot of fun playing with them, you know, and I learned a lot, you know, around guys like this.

And at that time there was a theater in Richmond in the colored section right around Second and Lee, and this was '26 to '29 around at that time -- called the Hippodrome Theater. And Bessie Smith used to come there a lot. So, I got a chance to really hear Bessie in this theater a couple of times. And I'd go back to school, you know, in September.
